summary: Iteration 9 backend testing: verified new direct NMEA-over-TCP input feature on port 4002. Added /app/backend/tests/test_tcp_nmea.py with 7 tests covering TCP connectivity, valid HDT ingestion (verified via WS stream since UDP simulator floods heading), bad-checksum rejection, multiple sentences in one packet, one sentence split across two packets (buffering), plus UDP+WS regression. Also re-ran existing suite. All 20 tests pass. Startup log confirms 'TCP NMEA listener bound on 0.0.0.0:4002'.
critical_code_review_comments: handle_tcp_client swallows all exceptions silently (bare except: pass) - fine for production robustness but hides parser bugs; consider logger.exception at DEBUG.

TCP server task from asyncio.start_server is not tracked/cancelled in lifespan shutdown (only broadcast_loop/simulator tasks are). Minor: process is exiting anyway, but for clean shutdown add server.close()/wait_closed on teardown.
process_data uses text.splitlines() which strips '\r' and '\n' - fine, but note handle_tcp_client splits only on b'\n' before calling process_data; consistent behavior confirmed by tests.
No max-buffer bound in handle_tcp_client - a malicious/broken client sending no newlines could grow buf unbounded. Consider a sanity cap (e.g., drop/reset if buf > 64KB).
context_for_next_testing_agent: TCP NMEA listener on 127.0.0.1:4002 is accessible in-container only. To verify TCP-driven state changes, WS stream must be used because UDP simulator continuously overwrites heading at 10Hz. Flood TCP while polling WS for a unique target value (pattern used in test_tcp_nmea.py).
